questions.subtopic: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb form:
"The introduction of electronic case display boards in various district court complexes ___ significantly reduced public confusion."
questions.explanation: Sentence ka grammatical subject 'The introduction' (singular head noun) hai. 'of electronic case display boards in various district court complexes' intervening prepositional phrases hain jinhe ignore karna chahiye. Singular head noun 'introduction' ke hisaab se singular auxiliary 'has' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Identify the option that correctly completes the sentence:
"The senior judicial assistant, as well as his newly appointed colleagues, ___ present in the training room."
questions.explanation: 'As well as' ek parenthetical expression hai jo compound addition nahi karta. Verb hamesha FIRST SUBJECT ('The senior judicial assistant' [singular]) ke according decide hoti hai. Isliye singular past verb 'was' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Parenthetical Connectives & The First-Subject Rule
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Choose the grammatically correct auxiliary verb:
"Not only the software engineers but also the system administrator ___ working overnight to restore the court database."
questions.explanation: 'Not only ... but also' construction mein Proximity Rule follow hota hai. Verb 'but also' ke baad aane wale nearer subject ('the system administrator' [singular]) ke according select hoti hai. Isliye singular past auxiliary 'was' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Correlative Conjunctions & The Proximity Rule
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
In the following sentence, identify the segment containing a grammatical error:
"(A) Each of the forensic reports / (B) submitted by the investigation officers / (C) have been carefully scrutinized / (D) by the special division bench."
questions.explanation: Segment (C) mein error hai. Sentence ka grammatical subject 'Each' (singular distributive pronoun) hai. Iske sath singular auxiliary verb 'HAS been carefully scrutinized' aani chahiye, 'have been' proximity error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Distributive Singular Pronouns: Each, Every, Either of, Neither of
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb:
"The number of candidates appearing in the preliminary computer typing examination ___ grown exponentially this year."
questions.explanation: 'The number of + plural noun' ek specific numerical count ko denote karta hai, aur iska grammatical subject word 'The number' (singular) hota hai. Isliye singular auxiliary 'has grown' aayegi. Plural auxiliary 'have' 'A number of' ke sath lagti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: 'A Number of' (Plural) vs 'The Number of' (Singular)
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the options below:

options.text: Sunil is one of those advocates who has always defended constitutional liberties.
Sunil is one of those advocates who have always defended constitutional liberties.
Sunil is one of those advocate who has always defended constitutional liberties.
Sunil is one of those advocate who have always defended constitutional liberties.

questions.explanation: Option B is correct. 'One of those' ke baad plural noun 'advocates' aana mandatory hai (eliminating C and D). Relative pronoun 'who' ka antecedent 'advocates' (plural) hai, isliye relative clause ke andar plural verb 'HAVE always defended' aayegi (eliminating A).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: 'One of the' Relative Clause Concord vs 'The Only One'
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Error Spotting: 'The Only One' Relative Concord
questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"(A) Of all the candidates / (B) interviewed by the selection committee, / (C) Arvind is the only one who have cleared / (D) the high-speed bilingual typing barrier."

options.text: Arvind is the only one who have cleared

questions.explanation: Segment (C) mein error hai. Sentence mein 'THE ONLY ONE' clause aaya hai jo antecedent ko strictly single individual par restrict karta hai. Isliye relative clause ke andar singular verb 'has cleared' aani chahiye, 'have cleared' incorrect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: 'One of the' Relative Clause Concord vs 'The Only One'
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate auxiliary verb:
"The five-member judicial bench ___ divided in their opinions regarding the validity of the subordinate regulation."
questions.explanation: Sentence mein markers 'DIVIDED' aur plural possessive pronoun 'THEIR opinions' clearly indicate kar rahe hain ki bench ke members aapas mein bant gaye hain (Noun of Multitude). Is situation mein collective noun plural treat hota hai aur plural past auxiliary 'were' leta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Collective Nouns: Unitary Sense vs Divided Members
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Compound Subjects: Single Person with Single Article
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence from the following options:

options.text: The Secretary and Treasurer have submitted the annual financial statement.
The Secretary and Treasurer has submitted the annual financial statement.
The Secretary and the Treasurer has submitted the annual financial statement.
A Secretary and the Treasurer is submitted the annual financial statement.

questions.explanation: Option B is correct. Jab article 'The' sirf pehle title ('The Secretary') ke aage laga ho aur dusre title ('Treasurer') ke aage na ho, toh iska matlab dono designations ek hi vyakti hold karta hai (1 Person ➔ Singular Verb 'has submitted'). Option C mein dono ke aage 'The' hai isliye 'have' hona chahiye tha.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Compound Subjects with 'AND': Two Entities vs Single Notion
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate auxiliary verb:
"Where ___ the files containing the confidential judicial vigilance inquiry deposited?"
questions.explanation: Interrogative sentence mein auxiliary verb subject se pehle aati hai. True grammatical subject verb ke baad aane wala noun phrase 'the files' (plural head noun) hai. 'containing the confidential inquiry' participial modifier hai. Plural subject 'files' ke hisaab se plural past verb 'were' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Identify the incorrect part of the sentence:
"(A) More than one court clerk / (B) were severely reprimanded / (C) for mishandling the electronic record / (D) during the emergency audit."
questions.explanation: Segment (B) mein error hai. 'More than one + Singular Noun' construction formal English grammar mein strictly SINGULAR VERB leti hai. Isliye 'were severely reprimanded' ke bajaye 'was severely reprimanded' aana chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-11: 'Many a' & 'More than one' Idiomatic Concord
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Variable Indefinite Pronouns: SANAM Rule with Countable Noun
questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct verb:
"Some of the computer monitors installed in the e-filing center ___ already developing display flickers."
questions.explanation: SANAM variable pronoun 'Some' ke baad 'of the computer monitors' (plural countable noun) aaya hai. Rule ke according jab SANAM pronoun plural countable noun ko refer kare, toh verb strictly PLURAL ('are') hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Variable Quantity Indefinite Pronouns: The SANAM Complement Law
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Measurement & Distance: Continuous Block as a Unit
questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence from the following options:

options.text: Twenty kilometres are a long distance to travel every morning for work.
Twenty kilometres is a long distance to travel every morning for work.
Twenty kilometre are a long distance to travel every morning for work.
Twenty kilometres were a long distances to travel every morning for work.

questions.explanation: Option B is correct. 'Twenty kilometres' yahan ek single unbroken journey/distance ke roop mein express ho raha hai (indicated by 'a long distance'). Distance, time, aur money jab ek single unit represent karein, toh verb strictly SINGULAR ('is') hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09A: Quantities, Measurements, Time, Distance & Money as Single Units
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Complete the sentence with the appropriate verb:
"In the central computer server room, there ___ a high-capacity server and several automated backup power units."
questions.explanation: 'There' dummy introductory word hai. Post-verbal subject compound hai: 'a high-capacity server AND several automated backup power units' (1 server + multiple power units = plural compound subject). Plural subject ke sath plural verb 'are' aayegi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Inverted Word Order & Dummy 'There' Concord
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Spot the error in the sentence:
"(A) Every judicial clerk / (B) and every administrative assistant / (C) were present at the mandatory / (D) cybersecurity orientation workshop."
questions.explanation: Segment (C) mein error hai. Jab do ya do se zyada nouns 'Every' ya 'Each' se precede hote hain chahe wo 'and' se jude hon, tab bhi verb strictly SINGULAR aati hai. Sahi verb 'WAS present' hogi, 'were present' incorrect hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Distributive Singular Pronouns: Each, Every, Either of, Neither of
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.subtopic: Sentence Correction: Plural Title of Creative Work
questions.question:
Select the correct version of the sentence:
"Gulliver's Travels are an exceptional satire written by Jonathan Swift."

options.text: Gulliver's Travels are an exceptional satire written by Jonathan Swift.
Gulliver's Travels is an exceptional satire written by Jonathan Swift.
Gulliver's Travel are an exceptional satire written by Jonathan Swift.
Gullivers' Travel were an exceptional satire written by Jonathan Swift.

questions.explanation: 'Gulliver's Travels' ek single classic book ka proper title hai. Bhale hi iske title mein plural word 'Travels' hai, ye ek single literary work represent karta hai aur strictly SINGULAR VERB ('is') leta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb form:
"Practicing mock typing tests on bilingual keyboard layouts daily ___ essential for achieving 100% accuracy."
questions.explanation: Sentence ka subject Gerund phrase 'Practicing mock typing tests...' hai. Jab koi Gerund (-ing phrase) sentence ka subject banta hai, toh use hamesha ek single abstract activity maana jata hai aur singular verb ('is') lagti hai. 'Tests' ya 'layouts' prepositional objects hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence:
"His statistics regarding court pendency ___ highly reliable, but Statistics as an academic subject ___ difficult for him."
questions.explanation: Jab '-ics' wale words (jaise statistics) ke aage possessive pronoun ('His statistics') lagta hai, toh iska matlab 'data figures' (plural) hota hai ➔ 'ARE reliable'. Lekin jab wahi word academic discipline ke roop mein use hota hai ('Statistics as a subject') ➔ SINGULAR 'IS difficult'. Sahi pair 'are / is' hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
In the sentence below, identify which word or phrase is the TRUE grammatical subject governing the verb 'has':
"The heavy wooden box containing numerous ancient judicial seals and copper coins has been safely preserved in the treasury."
questions.explanation: Verb 'has been preserved' se puchein: 'What has been preserved?' Answer: 'The heavy wooden box'. 'Judicial seals' aur 'copper coins' participial modifier 'containing...' ke objects hain. True grammatical subject 'The heavy wooden box' (singular) hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Head Noun Isolation vs Intervening Prepositional Phrases
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13

questions.question:
Fill in the blank in this interrogative sentence:
"___ either the senior superintendent or the junior assistants verified the uploaded biometric records?"
questions.explanation: Questions mein auxiliary verb subject se pehle aati hai. Either...or mein proximity rule physically nearest subject par lagta hai. Yahan auxiliary position ke sabse paas 'the senior superintendent' (singular) hai! Isliye singular auxiliary 'HAS' aayegi ('Has either the senior superintendent or the junior assistants verified...?').
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Correlative Conjunctions & The Proximity Rule
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L13
